newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says jobless rate past peak but still high.
newsitem.headline: Japan says jobless rate past peak but still high.

text.p: Japan said on Friday the worst of its unemployment problem was over but there was little improvement in sight, with the jobless rate clinging stubbornly close to record highs.
The government announced that the nation's unemployment rate in January was unchanged from December at 3.3 percent, a shade below the record 3.5 percent seen last summer.
"The worst was over when the jobless rate rose to 3.5 percent last year, but it is difficult to expect a quick improvement in the job situation," a senior government official told reporters.
The jobs data showed that the number of people employed in the manufacturing sector rose 0.9 percent to 14.39 million in January, the first rise since last September.
The overall number of those in work rose for the 11th straight month in January, hitting 64.2 million.
Another closely watched employment figure, the jobs-to-applicants ratio, was unchanged at 0.76 in January. This means there were 76 job offers for every 100 applicants.

While Japan does not have the double-digit jobless rates of some Western countries, the climb in the rate above three percent since early 1995 has caused concern in a nation which has had minimal unemployment for most of the postwar era.
By comparison, the jobless rate in France is now about 12 percent, while the rates are at about 10 percent in Germany, seven percent in Britain and five percent in the United States.

Japan's economy has been struggling to recover from a slump that set in after the collapse of the 1980s economic "bubble" of inflated asset prices, forcing companies to cut costs and restructure their operations to maintain profits.

Economists said the labour market has been improving on the back of a gradual economic recovery but the jobless rate is unlikely to drop substantially as better economic prospects will encourage more people to voluntarily quit to seek new jobs.

"The economy is certainly improving. But it was slightly disappointing to see that there was no progress in the unemployment rate and the jobs-to-applicants ratio," said Yasushi Okuda, an economist at BZW Japan.
Economists said a planned increase in Japan's consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1 will slow down consumption slightly but the economy will likely pick up later this year.
But the government is more cautious about the outlook.

"The job situation has improved since last year, but we are not sure if it will keep improving as a planned rise in the consumption tax could have some effect on the economy," the government official said.

Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told a news conference on Friday that the latest economic data such as the jobless rate show that Japan's economy is brightening up, although uncertainties remain.
He said the number of people being forced to leave their jobs had been declining steadily.
